summary: This document defines an RTCP Extended Report block for reporting de-jitter buffer metrics, for use in a range of RTP applications.

eli5.summary: A de-jitter buffer smooths out uneven arrival of audio or video. This lets it report how well it is doing.

questions: what is a de-jitter buffer report
subtitle: An RTCP report block that tells a sender how the receiver's de-jitter buffer is configured and behaving.

tldr.problem: Real-time receivers hide network delay variation with a de-jitter buffer, but nothing in RTCP told the other side how that buffer was set up or how it was coping.
tldr.mechanism: The De-Jitter Buffer Metrics Block (block type 23) reports whether the buffer is fixed or adaptive and four delay values in milliseconds: nominal, maximum, high-water mark and low-water mark.
tldr.outcome: The figures describe terminal-related factors that can feed end-user quality-of-experience calculations. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 7005 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2013. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the definition of this block.

sections.title: A Report Block for the De-Jitter Buffer
sections.content:
RFC 7005 defines one new RTCP Extended Report block to augment those in RFC 3611. It provides information on de-jitter buffer configuration and performance, and it belongs to the class of transport-related end-system metrics defined in RFC 6792.

Real-time applications use a de-jitter buffer to absorb jitter on the path from source to destination. These metrics report how that buffer at the receiving end behaves. The RFC describes them as terminal-related factors that affect application quality and can be inputs when calculating quality-of-experience metrics.
sections.eli5: When music or video arrives unevenly, the player holds it briefly so it can be played smoothly. This report says how that holding is going.

sections.title: How a De-Jitter Buffer Works
sections.content:
A de-jitter buffer holds media data for a period after it arrives and before it is played out. Packets that arrive early are held longer. If packets arrive too early they may be discarded when there is no buffer space, and packets delayed too much may be discarded if they miss their playout time.

The buffer can be seen as a time window. The delay applied to packets that arrive on time is the nominal delay. The maximum delay is the delay applied to the earliest arriving packet that is not discarded, which marks the early edge of the window.

The RFC describes an idealized buffer: delay the first packet by D ms, then for each later packet compute r (RTP timestamp difference) and t (receive time difference) against the first packet. If r equals t the packet was on time, r less than t means late, r greater than t means early, and playout is delayed by D + (r-t). This assumes the sender and receiver clocks are synchronized.
sections.eli5: Imagine a bus stop where riders wait so everyone boards in an even stream. Early arrivals wait longer, and anyone too late misses the bus.

sections.title: Fixed and Adaptive Buffers
sections.content:
A fixed de-jitter buffer does not track network conditions. It has a fixed size, and packets leave it with a constant delay. Its nominal delay and its maximum delay are both constants.

An adaptive de-jitter buffer follows changes in network delay and has variable size or delay. It can start with a low nominal delay to reduce the delay a user perceives, and then extend the late edge of the window (and possibly retract the early edge) if a significant proportion of packets arrive late and are discarded.
sections.eli5: A fixed waiting room is always the same size. An adaptive one grows when many people show up late and can shrink again.

sections.title: The De-Jitter Buffer Metrics Block
sections.content:
The block has block type BT=23 and a Block Length of 3. Its fields are:

  • I (2 bits): the Interval Metric flag. Here the metrics can only be sampled, so senders MUST NOT use I=00, I=10 or I=11, and a receiver MUST discard a block that has them. Sampled (I=01) is the only valid value.
  • C (1 bit): 0 for a fixed buffer, 1 for an adaptive buffer.
  • DJB nominal (16 bits): current nominal delay in milliseconds for packets arriving exactly on time. MUST be provided for fixed and adaptive buffers.
  • DJB maximum (16 bits): current maximum delay in milliseconds for the earliest arriving packet that would not be discarded. MUST also always be provided.
  • DJB high-water mark and DJB low-water mark (16 bits each): the highest and lowest nominal delay in milliseconds during the reporting interval. They MUST be provided for adaptive buffers, and for fixed buffers MUST be set to DJB maximum.

Each value is unsigned. If a measured value exceeds 0xFFFD, 0xFFFE MUST be reported to indicate over-range. If the measurement is unavailable, 0xFFFF MUST be reported.

The block refers by SSRC to a Measurement Information Block (RFC 6776) and MUST be sent in the same compound RTCP packet as that block. Otherwise it MUST be discarded.
sections.eli5: The report is a short form with a tick box for fixed or adaptive, and four numbers for how long packets wait. Special numbers mean too big to count or not measured.

sections.title: SDP Signaling
sections.content: Use of the block can be signaled with the SDP rtcp-xr attribute of RFC 3611. The RFC adds one new xr-format value, de-jitter-buffer. XR blocks MAY also be used without prior signaling. In offer/answer use, the RFC 3611 rules for unilateral rtcp-xr parameters apply.
sections.eli5: Before a call, a device can announce that it is happy to send this report by using its short name, de-jitter-buffer.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA assigns block type value 23 to the De-Jitter Buffer Metrics Block in the RTCP XR Block Type Registry, and registers the SDP parameter de-jitter-buffer.

On security, the RFC believes the block introduces no new considerations beyond those in RFC 3611. Because the block carries no per-packet statistics, the confidentiality risk described in paragraph 3 of Section 7 of RFC 3611 does not apply.
sections.eli5: The report only gives overall numbers, not details about each packet, so it gives away very little.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval Metric flag; only sampled values are valid.

fields.name: resv
fields.desc: Set to zero by senders, ignored by receivers.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: DJB high-water mark
fields.desc: Highest nominal delay in the interval.

fields.name: DJB low-water mark
fields.desc: Lowest nominal delay in the interval.
